output_text: {"action":"answer","expression":"","queries":[],"pages":[224,300],"status":"answered","answer":"Both aim to shift leverage away from data controllers and toward individuals or data contributors, but by different means. Personal-data portability gives individuals choice and control by enabling them to obtain and transfer their data to another collector or user; it is intended to reduce consumer-data lock-in and rebalance the relationship with controllers. A legally constituted data trust instead pools individuals’ legal rights in a shared intermediary, allowing them to negotiate collectively with larger controllers. Its trustees have a fiduciary duty to steward the data impartially, prudently, transparently, and with undivided loyalty to beneficiaries, following the trust’s governance rules.","citations":[{"page":224,"region_label":"Paragraph headed “Requiring data portability” (right column)","bbox":[0.566,0.642,0.934,0.911],"quote":"The right to personal data portability is designed to facilitate data transfers with the aim of increasing an individual’s choice and control over data about them.
